messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: alert: multiple services reporting OTLP export failures to Honeycomb (exporter=otel/honeycomb) — ingestion 429s & connection errors across eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Alert started at 1765823978. Paging on-call.

maria.cheng: seeing the same in prod traces UI — entire time range from ~09:55 is missing spans, looks like exporter batch flush failing. customers reporting missing traces in Console.

ash.patel: oncall here. confirming Honeycomb ingest 429 in the exporter logs:
```
2026-03-15T09:56:02Z ERROR exporter/honeycomb: post https://api.honeycomb.io/v1/indicators: 429 Too Many Requests
failed_batches=12 queued=420
```

james-ops: I can flip fallback exporter to S3 for the most noisy services (ingest-proxy + api-gateway) to avoid total data loss. We should also lower sampling rate temporarily.

sean.support: customer impact: two enterprise customers (acme-corp, finlytics) pinged support complaining that traces disappeared for several transactions. They're asking if data will be recovered.

ash.patel: action plan: 1) hit Honeycomb status and open ticket, 2) turn on local/buffered exporter for critical services, 3) reduce sample rate to 1% for non-critical hosts, 4) notify customers and document in incident page. doing step 1 now.

honeycomb-status-bot: Honeycomb status: Partial degradation — Trace ingestion experiencing rate limiting in eu-west-1 and us-west-2. See https://status.honeycomb.io/incidents/otlp-rate-limit-2026-03-15

maria.cheng: opened support ticket with reference 2026-03-15-REDWOOD-OTLP. Honeycomb says they're throttling due to transient backlog; they recommend backoff/retry and buffering on client side.

james-ops: rolling a config change to set HONEYCOMB_BACKEND=buffered_file for svc-api and svc-ingest on prod-1 and prod-2. Command:
```bash
kubectl set env deploy/svc-api HONEYCOMB_BACKEND=buffered_file -n prod
kubectl rollout restart deploy/svc-api -n prod
```

sean.support: creating a short customer-facing note in status.redwood.ai: "We're seeing trace export issues to Honeycomb causing gaps in trace data. We are buffering data and working with Honeycomb; logs and metrics are unaffected."

maria.cheng: also enabling reduced sampling for workers: setting ENV OTEL_SAMPLE_PROBABILITY=0.01 for non-critical. Patching config in configmap:
```yaml
traces:
  sampler: probabilistic
  probability: 0.01
```

sre_oncall: will monitor exporter queue sizes after the buffered backend flips. If queue > 1M events we throttle ingestion locally to avoid disk exhaustion. Creating alert: exporter_queue_bytes > 500MB -> ops page.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: page sent to pd-oncall@sre with severity=high. Acknowledged by user ash.patel at 1765824050.

ash.patel: update: buffered backend enabled on svc-api and svc-ingest in prod-1. Exporter queue rising but stable. Honeycomb ticket updated; they say they'll increase throughput within next 30m.

james-ops: started manual back-fill/export for last 30m spans from local buffer into an internal S3 bucket (we'll replay to Honeycomb after they lift throttles). Kickoff command: `./scripts/otlp-buffer-replay --src=/var/lib/otel/buffer --dest=s3://redwood-otel-backups/prod/1765824000/`

sean.support: posted update to customers and support thread. Customers were told: we are buffering traces and will attempt a replay; no logs/metrics affected.

maria.cheng: temporary mitigation seems to be preventing data loss for critical services. Console traces still show a gap until the replay completes. Setting incident severity to P2 -> P1 if customers escalate.

sre_oncall: handoff: my shift ends in 28m. If Honeycomb doesn't resume and we can't keep buffer stable, escalate to Eng Infra for emergency disk provisioning. I'll hand this to ash.patel.

ash.patel: taking over. I'm going to add a rate-limiter on emitter side to smooth bursts. Patch in flight.

honeycomb-status-bot: update: We have cleared backlog in eu-west-1, partial backlog in us-west-2 remains. ETA for full recovery: ~20–30 minutes.

james-ops: replay job completed for svc-api (30m window). Uploaded to S3 and queued replay to Honeycomb — awaiting acceptance.

maria.cheng: note for postmortem: root cause likely Honeycomb ingestion throttling due to a multi-region backlog; we had limited local buffering on some services and no uniform fallback. Recommend: document buffered_file backend across all services, increase default buffer size, and add observed exporter_queue_bytes dashboards.

sean.support: closing customer follow-ups for now — customers acknowledged the update and are waiting for replay confirmation.

ash.patel: final: Honeycomb confirmed acceptance of replayed batches for eu-west-1; us-west-2 still processing. Moving incident to monitoring mode. Creating incident page: https://redwood.atlassian.net/incident/RI-2026-03-15-otel-honeycomb.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. If export errors resume, this thread will be reopened automatically.

maria.cheng: assigning postmortem to eng-ml and eng-runtime. I'll draft playbook changes.

sre_oncall: handoff complete to ash.patel at 1765825200.

ash.patel: thanks team. I'll own follow-ups and the playbook update. :thumbsup:
